scope: Community Core privacy review readiness; engineering is not reopened

facts: User-authored payload purge is scheduled within 7 days after immediate irreversible account/community removal.
Operational detail is scrubbed at 90 days.
There is no fixed 365-day elevated tier.
D4 moderation/security/legal holds are the only Product-approved exception and must remain justified.
Creator identity is anonymized/private immediately.
Owned works are hidden/deleted from Community access and search immediately.
Comments are replaced with [deleted] and marked deleted.
Saved items, follows, reactions, notification deliveries, and WandAccount-DDVProfile links are deleted immediately.
Auth identity is retired and provider-account cleanup is queued.
PUBLIC published clear works are discoverable and directly accessible.
UNLISTED published clear works are directly accessible when the identifier/link is known but are not public discovery results.
PRIVATE works are owner/staff only.
Linked DDV Profile rows are owner/staff only.
Reports are reporter/staff; moderation cases/actions and audit events are staff-only.
Observed staging media and Preset buckets are private.
Community media read access is authorization-gated and uses a signed URL with 300-second lifetime.
Community media responses use Cache-Control private, no-store.
Non-staging Community/WEP bucket configuration fails closed if required explicit bucket configuration is missing.
Restore is quarantine-first.
Recovery Deletion Ledger is outside the primary rollback domain and limited by contract to deletionEventId, accountId, requestedAt.
Ledger retention target is 90 days.
Promotion is blocked if deletion reconciliation is unavailable or incomplete.
Actual production backup/storage providers and restore drills remain pending.
Wand does not claim provider-controlled backups/logs/email copies obey the primary 7-day/90-day timers.
Production Supabase plan and independent Storage recovery provider remain unselected.
Material provider retention and region/cross-border facts must be bound and disclosed before final Privacy approval.

evidence: Account deletion removes public.wand_account_ddv_profiles rows.
Account deletion does not delete or revoke the corresponding public.ddv_profiles row.
ddv_profiles retains binding_key_hash unless another process changes it.
No canonical definition was found for binding_key_hash derivation or verification_evidence_ref lifecycle.
requiredDecision: Define the raw value represented by binding_key_hash and the exact one-way construction, including salt/pepper/key-management assumptions.
Define whether the retained hash can be linked or brute-forced from DDV identifiers.
Define verification_evidence_ref contents/location and deletion lifecycle.
Choose the post-unlink/account-deletion behavior for orphan ddv_profiles: delete, revoke+null hash, or documented minimized retention with a purpose/horizon.

evidence: The model enforces at most three linked DDV profiles.
No ordinary self-service link correction/unlink command was found in the reviewed Community source.
Account deletion removes the account-to-DDV-profile link.
requiredDecision: Decide how a Wizard corrects a mistaken or obsolete link without deleting the entire Wand Account.
Determine whether unlink/rebind is required by the launch jurisdictions or Product policy.

evidence: UNLISTED published clear works are direct-readable by anon/authenticated callers who know the work identifier/link.
UNLISTED works are not public discovery results.
requiredDecision: User-facing visibility copy must say unlisted means link/identifier access, not private.
Terms/Privacy wording must not imply only the owner can read unlisted work.

evidence: No canonical minimum-age, minor-consent, or age-assurance launch policy was found.
The service includes user accounts, profiles, media, comments, publishing and moderation.
requiredDecision: Define intended launch audience and jurisdictions.
External Legal must determine whether COPPA, DSA minor protections, or other child-privacy rules apply and what age/consent/assurance flow is required.

evidence: Production Supabase project/plan does not exist.
Independent Storage recovery provider is TBD.
Current D6/D7 are design contracts, not provider-specific runtime evidence.
requiredDecision: Bind actual production provider, plan, region, backup/log retention, subprocessor/DPA/transfer terms and Storage recovery provider before final Privacy approval.

evidence: Report detail, moderation action reason/state, retention-hold reason and some audit metadata can contain free text/JSON.
These are restricted by RLS/staff boundaries and operational detail is minimized at the 90-day stage.
requiredDecision: Adopt operator guidance to avoid copying unnecessary personal/sensitive information into free-text fields.
Legal/Privacy must define when an active case/hold justifies retention beyond the normal scrub.

evidence: Contract field set is minimized.
External storage/encryption/access logging and 90-day deletion are not yet production-implemented.
requiredDecision: Select external rollback-independent storage and prove encryption, operator-only access, auditability, expiry and restore reconciliation.

evidence: Community upload storage keys are prefixed by the Auth subject.
Buckets are private and read access is signed/authorized.
Content payload is purged within 7 days under the approved D1 design.
requiredDecision: Privacy should explicitly accept the provider-subject prefix as a short-lived backend pseudonymous identifier or request an opaque identifier migration.

evidence: Account deletion exists and is proven.
No single canonical launch workflow for access/export/correction/objection requests was found.
requiredDecision: After launch jurisdictions are fixed, define required access/correction/export/objection/appeal workflows and response channels.

evidence: private.provider_cleanup_jobs retains provider_subject while provider deletion is pending.
The field is needed to identify the provider account to delete.
Completed provider-cleanup jobs are removed by the operational scrub.
requiredDecision: Privacy should record the provider-subject retention purpose as deletion execution/retry only and disallow secondary use.
